info.title: AuditManager PC-01 API
info.summary: The exact PC-01 journey: one project, one AR PDF, one text-consistency run, one CSV.
info.description:
Frozen at Gate A so `A5` can generate a typed client and `B6` can implement routers against a fixed shape, without either waiting on the other.

Resealed 2026-09-18 under owner ruling `R-3`: every operation here requires a bearer credential, declared once at the document root under `components.securitySchemes.bearerAuth`. The scheme names the seam and never its implementation. The operational liveness and readiness plane is outside `/api/v1`, carries no product meaning and needs no credential.

What this surface deliberately does not have: tenancy, WebSocket or server-sent events; an export resource, export identity or export polling, because a synchronous read creates nothing; and any endpoint outside the eleven capabilities `P2-API-01` enumerates, other than the credential exchange the authorization seam needs, which `W34-CONTRACT` adds below, the aggregate dashboard read `R-44` adds in `W46-SEAL`, further below still, and the account and registration operations `W49-SEAL-01` adds at the end. Roles and a per-client throttle on the unauthenticated registration operations were on this list until `R-55` and `R-56` ruled them in; the last reseal below says what each is.

Three rules hold everywhere and are not repeated per operation:

1. **Opaque identity.** Every identifier is `<prefix>_<ULID>` from `contracts/domain/v1/identifiers.json`, and every path parameter carries the pattern for its entity. No response body, header or error detail ever contains a bucket name, object key, filesystem path, URL to internal storage, credential, prompt or model payload.
2. **One failure shape.** Every non-2xx response is the `ErrorEnvelope` of `contracts/domain/v1/error-envelope.schema.json`, its `error_code` drawn from the twenty-three-code catalog and its `retryable` pinned to the catalog value for that code. A caller never infers retryability from the HTTP status.
3. **Correlation.** Every response carries `X-Correlation-Id`. A caller may supply one on the request; the edge assigns one when the caller does not.

Run state uses the contract vocabulary. The success terminal of an `AuditRun` is `published`. `succeeded` is a `StageResult` status on a different aggregate and never appears as a run state.

Resealed 2026-09-18 under owner ruling `R-5`, which closes `DEBT_REGISTER.md` `D-16` and `D-21` together. Three list operations -- `listDocuments`, `listVersions` and `listRuns` -- make published work reachable after a page reload: before them every read below the project list needed an identifier the client was already holding, so a reloaded screen could reach nothing that survived in the database and the store. And `RunStatus` gained `cost_micros`, `cost_basis` and `model_call_count`, so what a run spent is readable by a user for the first time. Each listing is a `GET` of the collection its parent creates into, pages with the same `cursor` and `limit` and returns the same `{items, page}` envelope as `listProjects`. No error code was added: an unknown parent is the catalog's `not_found` and a malformed cursor is `validation_failed`.

Amended 2026-09-18 under owner ruling `R-8`, which closes `DEBT_REGISTER.md` `D-18`. The domain catalog gains one code, `staged_upload_lost`, and the `ErrorCode` enum below carries it: twenty-one becomes twenty-two. Two blob-store failures demanding opposite operator responses -- *stop, the instance was restored wrong* against *retry the upload* -- both answered `conflict` with `aggregate_type` `Blob`, so their envelopes were byte-identical apart from `correlation_id`. A widened `safe_detail_keys` was offered and rejected, because a detail key cannot fix `retryable`: the envelope reads that flag from the catalog for the reported code, so only a separate code carries a separate value. **No path, operation or schema changed** -- that amendment moved none of the three counts -- and the new code travels on the `503` every staging write already declares.

Resealed 2026-09-22 by `W34-CONTRACT`. `R-3` declared the seam and left no way to get through it: the document required a bearer credential on every operation and described no operation that hands one out, so the only caller this surface admitted was one already holding a credential from somewhere the document does not name. One operation closes that -- `issueToken`, `POST /auth/token` -- and it is a credential *exchange* and nothing more: a login and a password in, an opaque credential and its lifetime out. It is the single operation whose `security` is the empty requirement, because requiring a credential to obtain one is a closed door with a handle on the inside.

**What this reseal deliberately did not add, because `T-6` forbade it.** No issuer, no discovery URL, no flow, no `bearerFormat`; and, until `R-55` superseded that part of `T-6` for the scope the `W49-SEAL-01` reseal below describes, no vocabulary of what a subject may do. The returned `token` is a string this document states no structure for; the deployment decides what it is, and the operations keep working when that decision changes. No error code was added either: an unaccepted login and password pair is the catalog's `authentication_required`, a malformed body is `validation_failed`. `permission_denied` is **not** declared here, because it means an authenticated subject refused a resource and this operation has no authenticated subject in it -- it is the operation that produces one. That reseal added one path, one operation and two schemas, and the sentence that stated the totals it produced has been rewritten as this delta: a reseal's own arithmetic stops being true at the next reseal, and `tests/contract/api_v1/test_surface_counts_in_prose.py` reads every such claim in this block against the live document. The totals are stated once, below.

Resealed 2026-09-22 by `W38-KB` under owner ruling `R-24`, which was ruled against the recommendation the owner was given: a client-side walk over runs and findings is cheaper and lives only as long as the alpha, and a listing operation costs a reseal and outlives it. One operation closes it -- `listDecisions`, `GET /decisions` -- because `listDecisionHistory` reads the history of **one** finding and nothing in this document enumerated decisions at all, so the knowledge base `R-23` requires had no source but a walk over every run. It is a projection in the sense `ADR-0012` fixes and creates nothing. Two component schemas were added, `DecisionRecord` and `DecisionRecordPage`; no parameter was, because `category` and `verdict` already exist and already mean the finding's category and the finding's current verdict. No error code was added: a malformed cursor is the catalog's `validation_failed`, an absent or refused credential is `authentication_required`, and there is no `404` on it at all -- the path addresses no parent identity, so an empty journal is an empty page. That reseal added one path, one operation and two schemas.

Resealed 2026-09-23 by `W39-REVOKE` under owner ruling `R-26`, which rules four account guards into the alpha. This is the one of them that **cannot be added later**: the other three make an account weak now and are fixed by adding them, while a credential already issued is permanent until it expires, and no later work reaches one sitting in somebody's browser. One operation closes it -- `changePassword`, `POST /auth/password` -- and it carries revocation with it, because the two share a mechanism: the account's credential generation is raised by the same write that stores the new digest, which is what makes every credential minted under the old password stop being accepted.

**What this does not add.** No response schema: a credential and its lifetime is one shape and `IssueTokenResponse` already names it. No error code: a wrong current password is the catalog's `authentication_required` and a new password that is the current one is `validation_failed`. No revocation operation: taking credentials away from accounts whose passwords nobody is changing is an operator's action on the deployment, and publishing it would have required deciding who may revoke whom, which this document then had no way to say. Since `W49-SEAL-01` an administrator's changes that take an account's rights away -- archive, a role change, a password reset -- revoke that account's credentials as part of the change, still without an operation of its own. One path, one operation and one schema. The surface moved to 15 / 18 / 51.

Resealed 2026-09-23 by `W42-SEAL` under owner rulings `R-37` and `R-29`, and it is the first reseal here that adds no path and no operation. **No path, operation or schema moved: still 15 / 18 / 51, exactly as before.** Three things change and each is a *description* or a *property of an existing schema*, which is precisely why it still costs a reseal -- the conformance gate drops descriptions as annotation under `N4`, so nothing but this document carries them to a reader, and `D-18`'s four documents move together or the frontend reads a contract the backend does not serve.

`R-37`, and `DEBT_REGISTER.md` `D-86`: `DecisionEvent.author_label` and `DecisionRecord.author_label` described themselves as *"one configured local reviewer label ... a label, not a subject identity"*. Since wave 41 that was false -- the server writes the authenticated reviewer, not a constant -- and the owner has now ruled that what it writes is the reviewer's **display name** rather than their login, because this is the field another reviewer reads on a decision somebody else took. **The schema does not move**: same type, same `minLength: 1`, same `maxLength: 128`. The sentence was wrong twice over and is corrected in both copies; `DecisionRecord` restates `DecisionEvent`'s properties rather than composing them with `allOf`, so a reseal that corrected one would have left `listDecisions` still describing the field falsely. An account that has chosen no display name records its login, which is a server-held string the reviewer typed and is 1..100 characters, inside this field's bounds by construction.

`R-29`, and `D-46`: `RunStatus` gains one optional property, `terminal_detail`. A `failed` run could say that a dependency was unavailable and could not say **which**, because the catalog's `safe_detail_keys` live on the `ErrorEnvelope` and a 200 run reading is not an error envelope. It is the same shape and the same rule as `ErrorEnvelope.details` -- safe scalar classifiers, restricted to the keys the domain catalog declares for the reported code -- applied to the code in `terminal_reason` instead of to the one in `error_code`, and it is present only beside a `terminal_reason` because the allowlist that bounds it is a property of that code. **No component schema was added**, because the shape is declared inline exactly as `ErrorEnvelope.details` is, and **no error code was added**: a distinct code for a replay miss was the row's other option and is a second reseal, which the owner did not take. The domain catalog did not grow in that reseal. The true sentence this makes sayable is *your document is fine, the provider is fine, this deployment has no recording for it*, which `R-30` made the ordinary case by putting the alpha stand in `recorded` mode. Two migrations carry the storage: `0009_reviewer_display_name` and `0010_run_terminal_detail`.

Resealed 2026-09-25 by `W45-BLOCKS`. One operation is added -- `getVersionBlocks`, `GET /versions/{version_uid}/blocks` -- the first half of `R-23`'s block markup: `page_geometry_extraction` writes a real `bbox` per extracted text line and this operation reads it back, keyed by `version_uid` rather than by `run_id` because the stage carries no model and no provider reference and its output is a deterministic property of the version, identical across every run that reaches it. It answers `404` for an unknown version and, for a known one, `status: "produced"` or `status: "not_produced"` -- absent is not empty, and a version whose geometry has not yet been derived answers the same `blocks: []` as one that genuinely has none, distinguished only by `status`. It carries no crops: the stage's second artifact, the page-crop manifest, is unconditionally empty in this pipeline and is not exposed here at all. Two component schemas are added, `VersionBlockIndex` and `BlockGeometry`; no error code was added, because the only refusal this operation needs, `not_found`, was already in the catalog.

Resealed 2026-09-25 by `W46-SEAL` under owner rulings `R-40` and `R-44` (`docs/program/OWNER_RULINGS_2026-09-17.md` section 3.15). Two things land together because `R-40` ruled both halves in, against the cheaper recommendation the drafting session gave: the field and its aggregation in one wave.

`UploadDocumentRequest.section` and `DocumentVersion.section` are added, both optional, drawing from the new `ProjectSection` enum -- legacy's fourteen project sections (`D-56`). The field lives on the document, not the version or the project: it classifies what a document is, not which revision of its bytes is being read, and a project holds many sections rather than being one. It is optional rather than required because this column starts with no rows to backfill and forcing every caller, `tests/e2e/**` among them, to name a section it may not know would fabricate a classification -- a document nobody has classified yet is a real state and is never defaulted to one of the fourteen.

One operation is added -- `getDashboardSummary`, `GET /dashboard` -- under `R-44`, the integrator's decision against the cheaper path: three of the four dashboard panels are already reachable by walking `listProjects`, `listDecisions` and `listRuns`, and the ruling is that the reseal this wave opens anyway should carry one aggregate read serving all four rather than three client-side walks a later aggregate read would only delete. It takes no parameter at all -- not a `project_uid`, not a date range, not a filter -- because a parameterised version of this operation would be a second, generic query surface over data three narrower operations already answer; what it answers is fixed: the operational shape of the whole deployment, right now. Every panel preserves absent is not empty: every `Verdict` and every `RunState` appears even at a count of zero, every one of the fourteen frozen sections appears in `section_breakdown` even with no documents, and the documents nobody has classified yet are their own row rather than folded into one of the fourteen. Seven component schemas are added -- `ProjectDocumentCount`, `VerdictCount`, `RunStateCount`, `RunActivitySpend`, `RunActivity`, `SectionDocumentCount` and `DashboardSummary` -- plus `ProjectSection`, eight in total. No error code was added: `getDashboardSummary` declares no `404`, because it names no parent identity to be missing, and no `422`, because it takes no parameter a caller could get wrong. That reseal added `/dashboard`, `getDashboardSummary` and the schemas named above.

Resealed 2026-09-29 by `W47-LOCK` under owner ruling `R-50` (`docs/program/OWNER_RULINGS_2026-09-17.md` section 3.17). `IssueTokenResponse` gains `is_default_credential`, boolean and required, answered by both operations that mint a credential. **No path, operation or schema moved**, because a property on a schema this document already carries adds no schema, and the domain catalog did not grow. That is why it is a reseal rather than an edit -- `D-18`'s four documents move together or the frontend reads a contract the backend does not serve.

**The owner took the expensive option on purpose, and this field is only half of it.** A deployment's seeded account is published in a migration's own docstring, so an unchanged password is a password everyone who has read the runbook already has. The field is the signpost: a client learns the state at the moment it signs in and can send that reviewer to a password screen. The lock is the other half and it is behaviour, not shape: while this field is `true`, every operation except `issueToken` and `changePassword` answers the `permission_denied` it already declares, carrying the detail key `required_capability` the domain catalog already permits it, with the value `password_changed`. **No error code was added and none was needed** -- naming the capability after the act rather than after the credential tells a caller what to do, and the credential already has a name in this response. A field without the refusal would leave the API open to the seeded password for any caller that skips the screens; a refusal without the field would leave the screens to discover the state by failing.

Resealed 2026-10-06 by `W49-SEAL-01` under owner rulings `R-55`, `R-56`, `R-59`, `R-60` and `R-61` (`docs/program/OWNER_RULINGS_2026-09-17.md` section 3.19). The alpha gains accounts a person can hold: an e-mail address as the sign-in identifier, a full name, a role set, registration requests an administrator decides, and account management. The operations named below are added with their paths and schemas, and the domain catalog gains one code and one safe detail key; no existing operation changes shape.

**Roles.** An account holds a set of `Role` values, `expert` and `admin`, and the server decides on every request what that set reaches -- a written register in the authorization seam, not a property of the credential and not a claim in it. Reading product data needs any active account with a complete profile; product changes (projects, uploads, runs, verdicts, comments, the export) need `expert`; account and request management needs `admin`. A refusal is the `403 permission_denied` every guarded operation already declares, with `required_capability` naming what is missing: `password_changed` (`R-50`), `profile_completed` (an account that has not given its names and e-mail yet reaches only `getMe`, `updateMyProfile` and `changePassword`), `role:expert` or `role:admin`. A change of an account's rights -- a role change, an archive, a restore, an administrator's password reset -- revokes every credential it holds, so it signs in again before it meets the new rights.

**The account itself:** `getMe` and `updateMyProfile` (`R-59`: an account created before this reseal keeps its login until it gives its e-mail and names, in one write). **Registration:** `submitRegistration` and `readRegistrationStatus` are reachable without a credential, like `issueToken`; the status read shows an applicant `pending` and nothing else, and answers every other pair -- a rejected application included -- with the generic `401` (`R-56` and its addendum of 2026-10-06). `listRegistrations`, `approveRegistration` and `rejectRegistration` are an administrator's. **Management:** `listUsers`, `getUser`, `updateUser`, `archiveUser`, `restoreUser`, `purgeUser` and `resetUserPassword`, all `admin`; archive is the normal removal and purge deletes only an archived account that nothing references (`R-61`).

**The catalog.** `rate_limited` (`429`, retryable) is added because the edge in front of `/api/v1` now throttles the unauthenticated registration operations per client, and a code invented at the edge is what the catalog's safety rules forbid; this application never raises it, and it is not declared on the operations: like the edge's own body-size refusal, it is answered before any operation is reached. `conflict` gains the safe detail key `conflict_reason`, an enum-like classifier -- `login_taken`, `request_pending`, `queue_full`, `account_referenced`, `last_admin` -- so the account and registration conflicts can be told apart without a free-text detail. Identities `usr` and `reg` enter `contracts/domain/v1/identifiers.json`, and the `app_user` and `registration_request` machines enter `state-machines.json`, which is what `state_transition_not_allowed` names. The domain catalog moved to twenty-three codes in W49.

Resealed 2026-10-08 by W52-SEAL-01: getProductVersion, listReleases and markReleaseNotesRead add the release boundary. That seal added the release operations and their shapes. All require an active complete account; a release read mark is the account's own state. The catalog and contract_version do not move. Stage C provides the release loader and runtime values.

W53-SEAL-01 adds durable execution declarations and optional RunStatus.reaudit_of_run_id. The seal declares the boundary; W53-EXEC-01 supplies behavior.

post.summary: Exchange a login and a password for a bearer credential.
post.description:
The only operation on this surface that is reachable without a credential, because it is the one that hands one out: its `security` is the empty requirement, which overrides the document root for this operation and for no other.

**What this operation says about the credential it returns: nothing.** The response carries an opaque string and how long it stays valid. Its structure, what it encodes, and where the deployment got it are the deployment's own, are not described anywhere in this document, and are never parsed by a caller -- the same rule that keeps `bearerFormat` off `components.securitySchemes.bearerAuth`. A deployment that replaces a static string with something else changes no operation here.

Nothing is created and nothing is changed, so there is no idempotency key: a repeat of the same exchange is a second exchange, not a replay of the first.

200.description: The credentials were accepted. The body carries the credential to present on every other operation and how long it stays valid.

post.summary: Change the signed-in account's password and revoke its old credentials.
post.description:
Two things happen here and they are one write. The account's password becomes the one supplied, and every credential this deployment ever minted for that account stops being accepted -- **including the credential this request presented**. A password change that leaves the old password's credentials working is a password change in name only, so the two are not offered separately and cannot land separately.

**Whose password changes is decided by the credential, never by the body.** There is no login property and there will not be one: the caller may change their own password and no other, and a login in the body would be an operation one caller could aim at another.

**The response is the replacement credential**, minted after the change, and the only one this account now accepts. It is answered rather than left to a second exchange because the caller's own credential was revoked by this very request: a `204` would leave them holding something already dead with no way to tell that from a failure.

The `403` is declared because every operation behind the seam declares it: `permission_denied` means an authenticated subject was refused, and a generated client needs a typed shape for it on every authorized operation. This operation does not raise it today: an account still on a default credential reaches it, so does an incomplete profile, and it needs no role.

Nothing is created, so there is no idempotency key. A repeat of the same request is refused by its own `current_password`, which is no longer current -- it is not replayed and there is no `409` here.

Revocation has no operation of its own on this surface. Ending a pilot -- taking credentials away from accounts whose passwords nobody is changing -- is an operator's action taken on the deployment; an administrator's changes that take an account's rights away (`archiveUser`, a role change through `updateUser`, `resetUserPassword`) revoke that account's credentials as part of the change.

200.description: The password was changed. Every credential minted for this account before this response -- including the one this request presented -- is refused from now on. The body carries the replacement.

201.description: The project was created, or the recorded outcome of an identical earlier request was replayed.

get.summary: List projects, newest first.

200.description: One page of projects.

post.summary: Upload one PDF and publish an immutable document version.
post.description:
The whole PC-01 ingest path. The accepted envelope is one unencrypted PDF, at most 25 MiB and at most 30 pages, every page carrying extractable embedded text. A scanned or image-only file, a password-protected file, a non-PDF, an oversize file, an over-page-count file and a companion or archive upload are each refused with `validation_failed` and a `constraint` detail. OCR is never silently substituted.

On success the version and its input manifest are immutable: there is no update or delete endpoint for either, and the database refuses both.

get.summary: List the documents of one project, newest first.
get.description:
One item per document, carrying the version the document currently points at -- the one a reader would open, stream or start a run against. A document with no published version is not listed, because there is nothing to address.

The item is a `DocumentVersion` because that is what `uploadDocument` publishes into this same collection: the `GET` of a collection returns a page of exactly what its `POST` returns, which is the rule `listProjects` follows against `createProject`. This surface has no separate `Document` resource and does not acquire one here.

An unknown project is `404`, never an empty page: "this project has nothing in it yet" is a different answer from "there is no such project".

200.description: One page of this project's documents.

get.summary: Read one published document version.

200.description: The version and its input manifest.

get.summary: Stream the PDF bytes for the viewer.
get.description: The server streams the bytes itself. It does not redirect and does not return a presigned link: a URL into object storage is exactly the internal address the contract forbids putting in a response, and it would also outlive the request that authorized it.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: Byte range, so the viewer can page a large document without fetching all of it.

200.description: The complete PDF.

Content-Length.description: Byte size of the published version.

get.summary: List the runs of one published version, newest first.
get.description:
Runs hang off the version because `startRun` takes a `version_uid` and nothing else that identifies anything -- the project is derived from it. This is the inverse of that direction and not a second way of addressing a run.

Each item is the whole `RunStatus`, identical to what `getRunStatus` answers for that run. There is no lighter list shape: a second shape of one resource is a second thing to drift.

An unknown version is `404`, never an empty page.

200.description: One page of this version's runs.

get.summary: Read the page-by-page block index derived for one published version.
get.description:
Keyed by `version_uid`, not by `run_id`. `page_geometry_extraction` carries no model and no provider reference, so its output is a deterministic re-derivation of the source bytes and the published text layer -- identical across every run of this version that reaches the stage successfully. Addressing it by run would ask a caller to already hold a run identity to read a fact about the document.

An unknown `version_uid` is `404`. A version that exists but whose most recent successful run never reached `page_geometry_extraction` -- or has no run at all -- answers `200` with `status: "not_produced"` and `blocks: []`; that is a different fact from a version whose geometry was produced and genuinely has no blocks, which answers `200` with `status: "produced"` and `blocks: []`. The two are the same bytes for `blocks` and different bytes for `status`, and a caller reads `status` to tell them apart -- never the length of `blocks`.

This operation does not carry crops. `page_geometry_extraction` also publishes a page-crop manifest, but this pipeline renders no visual detection and that manifest is unconditionally empty (`crop_policy: "none"`, `crops: []`); it is a separate artifact and is not exposed on this operation at all, rather than being shipped here as a field that is always `[]`.

200.description: The block index for this version, or its not-yet-produced status.

get.summary: List the published versions of one document, newest first.
get.description:
Every immutable version of one document, ordered by `version_ordinal` descending. The ordinal is a display and ordering value and is never an identity; the continuation token carries the opaque `version_uid` and nothing else.

An unknown document is `404`, never an empty page.

200.description: One page of this document's published versions.

post.summary: Start a text-consistency run over one published version.
post.description: PD-03, in the subset PC-01 exercises. A new idempotency key creates a run. The same key with the same payload returns the existing run and creates nothing, whatever state that run is in, terminal included. The same key with a different payload returns `idempotency_key_reuse` and creates nothing. A new key over a terminal run creates a new run and leaves the terminal one exactly as it was: a terminal run is never reopened.

202.description: The run exists. A replay under the same key and payload returns the same run and this same status.

get.summary: Read run state and per-stage state.
get.description: The polling target. `state` is the contract run state; `stages` carries one entry per stage the run scheduled, with the `StageResult` status vocabulary. A client stops polling on any terminal state.

200.description: Current run state.

get.summary: List the published findings of one run, with their evidence.
get.description: Published means grounded: every listed finding's quotations were verified present at their declared anchors. An ungrounded model item is not a finding, does not appear here and is retained only as run diagnostics.

200.description: One page of findings.

get.summary: Read one finding with its observation, evidence and provenance.

200.description: The finding detail.

post.description:
Append-only. Nothing is updated: an accept after a reject is a third event, and the current verdict is a projection over the stream. Replaying under one idempotency key appends exactly one event, which the database enforces rather than the handler promising it.

PC-01 emits `accept`, `reject` and `comment`. `revoke` is declared so the PD-01 revocation semantics stay implementable without a schema change; no PC-01 client offers it.

201.description: The appended event, and the projection that now follows from the stream.

get.summary: Read the decision history of one finding, oldest first.
get.description: Ordered by `(recorded_at, decision_id)`, which is a total order and is stable across pages. The server's row sequence is never exposed, in a field or inside a cursor.

200.description: One page of decision events.

get.summary: Read the decision journal across findings, newest first.
get.description:
Every expert decision this deployment has recorded, in one listing, with the finding context each event was recorded against. `listDecisionHistory` answers *what was decided about this finding*; this answers *what has been decided*, which no operation could answer before and which a client could otherwise reach only by walking every run and every finding.

**It is a projection and creates nothing.** `ADR-0012` holds: the current verdict, the reason aggregates and the knowledge-base views are rebuildable projections over the append-only ledger. Every property of `DecisionRecord` is rebuildable from `expert_decision_event`, `finding`, `finding_observation` and the `finding_current_verdict` projection, and this operation is the only place they are read together.

Ordered by `(recorded_at, decision_id)` **descending** - the newest decision first, as `listProjects` orders projects - and that is a total order, stable across pages. The server's row sequence is never exposed, in a field or inside a cursor.

`category` and `verdict` filter on the **finding**, exactly as they do on `listRunFindings`: the category of the finding the event was recorded against, and the verdict that now stands for it. Neither filters on the event. There is no parent identity in the path, so an empty journal is an empty page and never `not_found`.

200.description: One page of the decision journal.

get.summary: Download the CSV for one run.
get.description:
Synchronous. Nothing is created, so there is no export resource, no export identity and nothing to poll. Repeating the request returns byte-identical bytes.

The discriminator is the frozen `terminal_semantics.publishes_result` flag, not a hand-written state list (`OD-11`). A run whose terminal declares `publishes_result: true` - `published` or `partial` - is exported, with the degraded state carried explicitly in the `run_state` column rather than as a silent empty file. Every other state is refused with `state_transition_not_allowed`: a non-terminal run, and the terminal `failed`. `cancelled` is likewise not exportable and is unreachable in PC-01. `partial_result_not_publishable` is never emitted by this surface.

Bytes: UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, comma delimiter, CRLF line ending, RFC 4180 quoting. The column list and its order are frozen in `docs/program/P02_SEAMS.md` section 6.

200.description: The CSV for this exact project, version and run.

Content-Disposition.description: Attachment with a display file name built from opaque identifiers. The file name is presentation only and is never an identity.

get.summary: One aggregate read across the whole deployment: all four dashboard panels.
get.description: Documents per project, findings by verdict, run activity and spend, and the per-section breakdown -- computed server-side over the whole deployment, never walked client-side (`R-44`). Takes no parameter: it is not a filtered query over the data three narrower operations already answer (`listProjects`, `listDecisions`, `listRuns`), it is the fixed shape of the deployment right now. Absent is not empty throughout: every `Verdict` and `RunState` is present even at zero, every one of the fourteen frozen sections is present even with no documents, and the unclassified documents are their own row.

200.description: The whole deployment's operational shape, right now.

get.summary: Read the signed-in account.
get.description: The account the presented credential names: its login, names, role set and state. Reachable by an account still on a default credential and by an incomplete profile, because it is how a client learns either state; every operation that is not this one, `updateMyProfile` or `changePassword` answers an incomplete profile with `permission_denied` and `required_capability: profile_completed`. Nothing is created or changed.

200.description: The signed-in account.

patch.summary: Set the signed-in account's names, and complete its profile.
patch.description: **Completion** (R-59): an account whose profile is incomplete gives its names and -- unless its login already is one -- its e-mail address, and the names, the login and the completion are written in **one** update, so there is no instant at which the account has one without the other. **A complete profile** changes its names only; its login is fixed. An e-mail another active account holds is `conflict` with `details.conflict_reason: login_taken`. The account is the one the credential names, never one named in the body. No credential is revoked: names are not rights.

200.description: The account after the change.

post.description: Reachable without a credential: `security` is the empty requirement, as on `issueToken`. Records an application an administrator then approves or rejects; no mail is sent (R-56). The e-mail, the names and the password are validated first, then: an active account holding the login is `conflict` with `conflict_reason: login_taken`, a pending request for it `request_pending`, and 100 pending requests in all `queue_full`. That the first two tell a submitter a login is known is an accepted, registered limitation. Neither `401` nor `403` is declared: there is no credential to refuse and no subject to deny. The edge in front of this surface throttles it per client and answers `rate_limited` (`429`) itself, before the operation is reached; like the edge's own body-size refusal, that answer is not a response of the operation and is not declared here.

201.description: The application was recorded and is pending.

get.summary: List registration requests, oldest first.
get.description: Requires `admin`. Every request, or those in one status, ordered by `(submitted_at, request_id)`, with `pending_total` -- the number of pending requests whatever the filter.

200.description: One page of registration requests.

post.summary: Read whether a login and password pair proves a pending application.
post.description: Reachable without a credential, like `issueToken`, and called by a client after an exchange was refused. A pair that proves a **pending** application answers `{"status": "pending"}`. **Every other pair answers the same `401 authentication_required` a refused exchange gets** -- an unknown login, a wrong password, and a decided application, whose password was removed at the decision so that nothing can prove the pair. A rejected applicant is told nothing here (R-56 addendum of 2026-10-06); the reason is for administrators. Every path costs the same work, so the timing reveals nothing either, and refused reads are counted on the request with the sign-in brake's rules. `403` is not declared: there is no subject to deny. The edge throttles it per client and answers `rate_limited` (`429`) itself, before the operation is reached.

200.description: The pair proves a pending application.

post.summary: Approve a registration request and create the account.
post.description: Requires `admin`. In one transaction, with the request locked: the account is created from the request's login, names and password, with a complete profile and the roles the body names (at least one); the request is decided and its password removed. The same `Idempotency-Key` with the same payload replays the recorded outcome; with another payload it is `idempotency_key_reuse`.

200.description: The request as decided, naming the account it created, or the recorded outcome of an identical earlier request.

post.summary: Reject a registration request with a reason.
post.description: Requires `admin`. Decides the request as rejected with the reason, which is stored for administrators only, and removes its password. A request that is no longer pending is `state_transition_not_allowed` against `registration_request`. No account is created.

200.description: The request as decided.

get.summary: List accounts, ordered by login.
get.description: Requires `admin`. Every active account, or every account with `include_archived=true`, ordered by `(login, user_uid)`.

200.description: One page of accounts.

get.summary: Read one account.
get.description: Requires `admin`. One account, archived or not.

200.description: The account.

patch.summary: Change an account's names, its role set, or both.
patch.description: Requires `admin`. Names change without revoking anything; a change of the role set revokes every credential the account holds, so it signs in again and only then meets its new rights. An administrator cannot remove a role from themselves (`permission_denied`, no detail), and the last active account holding `admin` cannot lose it (`conflict`, `conflict_reason: last_admin`). An administrator naming an account whose profile is incomplete does not complete it: only the account itself gives its e-mail.

200.description: The account after the change.

delete.description: Requires `admin`. Irreversible (R-61): an **archived** account that nothing references is deleted with its roles; the request that created it keeps its row, and the login becomes free. An account that is not archived is `state_transition_not_allowed` against `app_user`; one that archived, granted or decided anything, or authored a decision, is `conflict` with `conflict_reason: account_referenced` and stays archived; oneself is `permission_denied`.

post.description: Requires `admin`. Archive is the normal removal (R-61) and is reversible: the account cannot sign in and every credential it holds is refused from its next request. Oneself is `permission_denied`; an archived account is `state_transition_not_allowed` against `app_user`; the last active account holding `admin` is `conflict` with `conflict_reason: last_admin`.

200.description: The account, archived.

post.description: Requires `admin`. Returns an archived account to active; it signs in again with its own password. An active account is `state_transition_not_allowed` against `app_user`; a login another active account took meanwhile is `conflict` with `conflict_reason: login_taken`.

200.description: The account, active.

post.summary: Set a temporary password for an account.
post.description: Requires `admin`. The account's password becomes the temporary one, held to the password policy; the account must change it at its next sign-in (`is_default_credential` becomes true), its sign-in brake is cleared, and every credential it holds is refused. Not oneself (`permission_denied`): an administrator changes their own password with `changePassword`. That the administrator knows the temporary password is a registered limitation.

200.description: The account, which must now change its password.

get.summary: Read the running product version.
get.description: Requires an active account with a complete profile. product_version comes from VERSION, build_id identifies this API process's content, and contract_version remains the API contract version.

200.description: The running product, build and contract versions.

get.summary: List visible releases and what is new.
get.description: Requires an active account with a complete profile. Returns releases at or below the running product version, highest revision per release, newest first with the archive last. whats_new contains only non-archive versions loaded after this account was created and above its read mark.

200.description: Visible releases and unread versions for this account.

put.summary: Mark release notes read through a version.
put.description: Requires an active account with a complete profile, including an administrator without the expert role. The credential names the account; the body cannot name another. A known version at or below the running product version raises its high-water mark; a lower or equal version is a no-op. Unknown or future versions are validation_failed. No idempotency key is required.

204.description: The account's read mark was raised or already covered this version.

get.summary: List Queue

200.description: The durable queue and dispatch pause state.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

get.summary: List Journal

200.description: The execution journal, newest first.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

200.description: The cancelled run or a replayed result.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

202.description: The newly accepted re-audit run or a replayed result.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

200.description: The queued job with its new priority.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

200.description: The durable dispatch pause state.

X-Correlation-Id.description: The correlation id for this request, assigned when the caller supplied none.

bearerAuth.description:
The authorization seam. Every operation in this document requires a bearer credential presented as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, except `issueToken`, `submitRegistration` and `readRegistrationStatus`, whose own `security` is the empty requirement: the credential exchange because it is what a caller with no credential uses to obtain one, and the registration pair because an applicant has no account yet.

**This declares the seam, not its implementation.** No issuer, no discovery URL, no flow and no token format appears here, and none may be added: the deployment decides them and the same operations must keep working when it does. What a subject may do is not carried by the scheme or the credential either: since `R-55` it is the account's role set (`Role`), which the server reads from the account on every request. `bearerFormat` is deliberately absent for that reason -- an opaque deployment token and an OIDC-issued JWT are both bearer credentials, and naming the format would pin the document to whichever one is current.

A request with no credential, or one the deployment does not accept, is `401 authentication_required`; so is an exchange whose login and password the deployment does not accept, which is the same refusal and not a second one. A credential the deployment accepts, for a subject not permitted this operation on this resource, is `403 permission_denied`, its `required_capability` naming what is missing (`password_changed`, `profile_completed`, `role:expert` or `role:admin`); authorization is decided server-side and the response never reveals the existence of a resource the caller may not see, so absence and refusal are reported as this surface's `404 not_found` where revealing them would leak.

Nothing outside `/api/v1` is covered. The operational liveness and readiness plane answers on its own port, carries no product meaning and needs no credential.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Client-supplied command key. Passed through to the owning command handler unchanged and never re-derived in the router. Never returned in a response body and never placed in an error envelope: it is a forbidden detail key.

CorrelationId.name: X-Correlation-Id
CorrelationId.description: Correlates this request with its diagnostic record. The edge assigns one when the caller does not supply it.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque continuation token from the previous page's `next_cursor`. Never parsed by a client and never constructed by one.

CategoryFilter.name: category
CategoryFilter.description: Restrict the page to one finding category.

VerdictFilter.name: verdict
VerdictFilter.description: Restrict the page to findings whose current projected verdict is this value.

RegistrationStatusFilter.name: status
RegistrationStatusFilter.description: Restrict the page to requests in this status.

CorrelationId.description: Present on every response, success or failure, so an operator can find the diagnostic record without the response carrying unsafe content.

AuthenticationRequired.description: `authentication_required`. No valid authenticated subject was presented: the request carried no bearer credential, or one this deployment does not accept, or -- on the credential exchange, which presents no credential by design -- a login and password pair this deployment does not accept. The response carries no hint about the addressed resource, so it is the same answer whether or not the resource exists.

PermissionDenied.description: `permission_denied`. The authenticated subject is not permitted to perform this operation on this resource. Authorization is decided server-side. This is the caller's rights and nothing else: a dependency that refuses the *application's* own credential is `dependency_credential_refused` on the 500 response, which is a server fault and not this one.

NotFound.description: The addressed aggregate does not exist or is not visible. The response never reveals the existence of a resource the caller may not see.

ValidationFailed.description: The request or payload violates a declared schema, enum, format or invariant. Nothing was created or changed.

UploadRejected.description: The upload failed the PC-01 input envelope (`validation_failed`) or its bytes did not match their declared checksum or size (`storage_integrity_error`). In both cases nothing was published: no version row, no manifest and no readable object.

StorageIntegrityError.description: Stored bytes do not match their declared identity.

RunInputInvalid.description: The declared analysis inputs are not structurally acceptable (`analysis_input_invalid`) or the request itself is invalid (`validation_failed`).

IdempotencyConflict.description: One of: `idempotency_key_reuse`, the same key with a different payload, which creates and changes nothing; `idempotency_key_in_progress`, the same key and payload still executing, which the caller retries under the same key and never re-issues under a new one; `idempotency_key_stale`, the recorded outcome is no longer available and is not guessed; or `conflict` for a uniqueness invariant with no more specific code.

RunNotExportable.description: `state_transition_not_allowed`. The run's terminal does not publish a result - a non-terminal run, or the terminal `failed` - so there is no download. A `partial` run is exported and is never refused here.

InternalError.description: An unclassified server fault, a declared run failure, or `dependency_credential_refused` -- a dependency refusing the application's own credential, which is a server-side configuration fault with no authenticated subject in it. The original internal code stays in protected diagnostics and never reaches this envelope.

DependencyUnavailable.description: `dependency_unavailable`, or since `R-8` `staged_upload_lost` on a write that stages bytes. The caller retries; nothing was partially applied. `idempotency_key_in_progress` is also retryable and is reachable on every write, so a caller reads `retryable` from the envelope, where the catalog pins it per code, and never infers it from the status or from a description like this one.

StateConflict.description: The change conflicts with durable state. `conflict` carries `details.conflict_reason`: `login_taken` (an active account holds the login), `request_pending` (a request for the login is already pending), `queue_full` (the pending queue is at its cap of 100), `account_referenced` (the account is referenced and cannot be purged) or `last_admin` (no active account would hold `admin`). `state_transition_not_allowed` names the `app_user` or `registration_request` machine with `details.machine`, `current_state` and `requested_state`. On an operation that takes an idempotency key the idempotency-key codes are reported here too.

ApprovalConflict.description: One of: `idempotency_key_reuse`, `idempotency_key_in_progress` or `idempotency_key_stale`, as on every keyed create; `state_transition_not_allowed` against `registration_request` when the request is no longer pending (of two concurrent approvals one wins and the other gets this); or `conflict` with `details.conflict_reason: login_taken` when an active account took the login meanwhile, which leaves the request pending.

FindingUid.description: Durable semantic issue identity, carrying expert history across reruns.

FindingObservationId.description: Immutable evidence emitted by exactly one run.

CorrelationId.description: Not an entity identity. Never a foreign key and authorizes nothing.

CostBasis.description: How well a published cost figure is known. `measured` means every provider call the figure sums reported its own cost; `estimated` means at least one did not, so the total is derived. The value is an aggregate over **every** call the figure spans and is never the last call's basis: a run whose first attempt replayed and whose second reported a cost is `estimated`.

IdempotencyKey.description: Not an entity identity. Never interpreted as, converted into or stored as a system identifier.

Sha256.description: A verification value, never an identity.

Cursor.description: Opaque pagination token. It encodes the sort key of the last item on the page and nothing else; it is never a database row number or sequence value.

next_cursor.description: Token for the next page, or null when this is the last page.

ErrorCode.description: Exactly the key set of contracts/domain/v1/error-codes.json.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The single externally visible failure shape, mirroring urn:auditmanager:domain:error-envelope:v1. `retryable` is pinned to the catalog value for the reported code; a caller never infers it from the HTTP status or the message.

message.description: Stable caller-safe sentence. No path, object key, URL, credential, token, prompt, payload, query or stack content.

details.description: Safe scalar classifiers only, restricted to the safe_detail_keys the catalog declares for the reported code. The catalog's forbidden key set is rejected.

RunState.description: The audit_run states of contracts/domain/v1/state-machines.json. The success terminal is `published`; there is no `succeeded` run state. `created` is transient and rarely observed by a client. `cancelled` is declared by the contract and is unreachable in PC-01, which has no cancel command.

StageStatus.description: StageResult statuses from contracts/analysis/v1. A `succeeded` stage carries no error; every other status carries one.

StageId.description: A canonical stage identity from contracts/analysis/v1/stage-registry.json. PC-01 schedules the first four.

ProviderMode.description: Whether the model call was made live or replayed from a recording. Visible in the UI and in the CSV, because a recorded run is not evidence of a live one.

FindingCategory.description: The only two questions PC-01 answers.

Verdict.description: The current projected verdict. `pending` when the ledger holds no verdict-bearing event, and after a revocation. `needs_manual_review` is declared for the closed union and has no PC-01 producer.

DecisionEventType.description: PC-01 emits accept, reject and comment. `revoke` is declared so PD-01 revocation stays implementable without a schema change.

ProjectSection.description: Legacy's fourteen project sections (`D-56`, `R-40`). A document with no section is not a fifteenth member of this enum -- it is `UploadDocumentRequest.section` or `DocumentVersion.section` absent, which is a different, equally real fact.

name.description: Display label. Not unique and not an identity.

file.description: One unencrypted PDF, at most 25 MiB and at most 30 pages, every page carrying extractable embedded text.

display_title.description: Optional display label. When absent the server derives one for presentation. Neither this nor the uploaded file name is ever an identity.

section.description: One of legacy's fourteen project sections, or absent when the document has not been classified.

InputManifestEntry.description: One role of the immutable input manifest. It carries a blob_id and a checksum and never an object key, bucket or URL.

DocumentVersion.description: A published, immutable input state. There is no endpoint that modifies one.

version_ordinal.description: Display and ordering value only. Never an identity and never accepted as a path parameter.

section.description: One of legacy's fourteen project sections, or absent when the document has not been classified.

source_filename.description: The uploaded file name, for display. Never an identity.

BlockGeometry.description: One derived block, one extracted text line. `block_id` is an anchor inside this artifact -- it matches `Evidence.block_id`'s pattern -- and is never a contract identifier.

block_ordinal.description: Position of this block within its page, starting at 0.

bbox.description: Points, top-left origin, y increasing downward -- see `bbox_unit` and `bbox_origin` beside it.

char_start.description: Document-global offset into the version's prepared text layer, counted in Unicode code points -- the same sequence `Evidence.char_start` indexes.

VersionBlockIndex.description: The page-by-page block markup derived for one version. Carries no crops: `page_geometry_extraction` also publishes a page-crop manifest, and this pipeline renders no visual detection, so that manifest is unconditionally empty and is a separate artifact this operation does not expose.

status.description: `produced`: a run reached `page_geometry_extraction` and this is its output, `blocks` may still be empty for a version that genuinely has none. `not_produced`: no run of this version has published this artifact yet -- absent, not empty -- and `blocks` is `[]` for that reason instead.

produced_by_run_id.description: The run whose `page_geometry_extraction` result this is. Null exactly when `status` is `not_produced`.

text_layer_sha256.description: Binds this block index to the exact prepared text layer its spans index. Null exactly when `status` is `not_produced`.

block_count.description: `len(blocks)`, carried rather than left for a caller to recompute.

provider_mode.description: Defaults to the server's configured mode. A client asking for `live` is asking to spend money against the OD-03 ceiling.

error_code.description: The typed reason a non-succeeded stage carries. Null exactly when the status is `succeeded`.

degradation_set.description: The explicitly recorded missing or degraded stage set. Non-empty exactly when the run is `partial`; a `published` run carries none.

terminal_reason.description: The catalog code a `failed` run terminated with. Null otherwise.

terminal_detail.description: D-46: safe scalar classifiers saying WHICH dependency a `failed` run terminated on, restricted to the `safe_detail_keys` the domain catalog declares for the code in `terminal_reason`. Present only beside a `terminal_reason`, because the allowlist that bounds these keys is a property of the reported code; absent when there is nothing to say, and never an empty object. The same shape and the same rule as `ErrorEnvelope.details`, applied to a 200 run reading rather than to a failure -- which is why it had to be added at all: a run reading is not an error envelope and carried no detail object. It classifies; it never identifies. No path, object key, URL, credential, token, prompt, payload or host appears here, and no error code was added to the catalog for it.

interrupted_reason.description: OD-10: a run left `running` by a crash is reconciled to `failed` with an explicit interrupted reason. There is no `interrupted` state.

diagnostic_observation_count.description: Ungrounded model items rejected by the grounding gate. They are not findings and appear in no finding list.

cost_micros.description: What this run spent at the provider, in millionths of the provider currency unit, as an integer. Never a floating-point money value. It is the sum of `cost_micros` over **every** `model_call` row of this run, including every retry attempt, because the per-run budget ceiling is enforced over the same span. Absent when the run made no provider call at all, which is a different fact from a cost of zero.

model_call_count.description: How many provider calls `cost_micros` sums. Published rather than left to be inferred: a reader who cannot see it cannot tell a run answered first time from one that was retried, and the two spent differently. Present exactly when `cost_micros` is.

Evidence.description: One verified quotation. `char_start` and `char_end` index the document-global character sequence of the prepared text layer, counted in Unicode code points after the declared normalization - see docs/program/P02_SEAMS.md section 4.

block_id.description: Secondary anchor into this version's block index. Not a contract identifier.

ObservationProvenance.description: What produced this observation. Checksums and identities only: never the prompt, the request or the response body.

Finding.description: A published finding. Every listed finding is grounded: its quotations were verified present at their declared anchors.

FindingDetail.description: One finding with its full current-verdict projection. Restates `Finding` rather than composing it with `allOf`: under JSON Schema 2020-12 an `additionalProperties: false` is evaluated against its own schema object's property annotations only, so an `allOf` branch over the closed `Finding` would reject the two properties the sibling branch adds. Both shapes stay closed, and tests/contract/api_v1 asserts this property set stays `Finding`'s plus exactly `latest_comment` and `decision_event_count`.

latest_comment.description: The comment of the most recent event carrying one, whatever its type.

finding_observation_id.description: The observation the expert actually reviewed. A verdict is recorded against the evidence in front of the reviewer, not against whatever the newest run later produced.

comment.description: Required for `comment`; optional on any other event type.

DecisionEvent.description: One appended event. Never updated and never removed.

verdict.description: The verdict this event carries, or null for a comment.

author_label.description: OD-12, as `R-37` now defines it: the display name of the reviewer who recorded the event -- the name they chose, or their login when they have chosen none -- derived server-side from the authenticated credential and **never** taken from a request body. It IS a subject identity: it names which reviewer judged, which is what `P04` needs and what one configured label for every reviewer could not give it. It still authorizes nothing: it is what the ledger records about who judged, not a permission anybody holds, and no client can choose it. The ledger is append-only, so an event keeps the label it was written with even after that reviewer is renamed.

DecisionRecord.description: One event of the decision journal, with the finding context it was recorded against. A rebuildable projection and never a source of truth: every property here is derived from `expert_decision_event`, `finding`, `finding_observation` and the `finding_current_verdict` projection, and nothing is stored in this shape. It restates `DecisionEvent`'s properties rather than composing them with `allOf`, for the reason `FindingDetail` states: under JSON Schema 2020-12 an `additionalProperties: false` is evaluated against its own schema object's property annotations only, so an `allOf` branch over the closed `DecisionEvent` would reject the properties the sibling branch adds.

verdict.description: The verdict this event carries, or null for a comment.

author_label.description: OD-12, as `R-37` now defines it: the display name of the reviewer who recorded the event -- the name they chose, or their login when they have chosen none -- derived server-side from the authenticated credential and **never** taken from a request body. It IS a subject identity: it names which reviewer judged, which is what `P04` needs and what one configured label for every reviewer could not give it. It still authorizes nothing: it is what the ledger records about who judged, not a permission anybody holds, and no client can choose it. The ledger is append-only, so an event keeps the label it was written with even after that reviewer is renamed.

finding_text.description: The observation's own words, as `FindingObservation.finding_text` carries them. It is the analysis's text and not this API's prose, so it is in whatever language the analysis produced.

decision_event_count.description: How many events the ledger holds for this finding, including this one. A count greater than one means the expert returned to the finding.

login.description: The caller's login, spelled the way the deployment spells it. Not an identity of this surface: it addresses nothing, appears in no path and is never a foreign key.

password.description: The secret presented with the login. It appears in no response body, no error detail and no diagnostic record.

token.description: The credential, presented on the authorized operations as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Opaque: this document states no format for it, and a caller that reads anything out of it has taken a dependency this contract does not offer.

expires_in.description: How long the credential stays valid, in seconds counted from this response. A lifetime and never a clock reading, so no clock has to agree between the two sides. A caller exchanges again before it elapses; an elapsed credential is `authentication_required` like any other the deployment does not accept.

is_default_credential.description: Whether the account this credential was just minted for is still on the password the deployment seeded it with. `true` says the password has never been changed; `false` says it has. It is a fact about the account's password and not a statement about what the subject may do -- what follows from it is declared where refusals are declared: every operation but this one and `changePassword` answers `permission_denied` with `required_capability: password_changed` while it is `true`. Required, not optional, because a caller that could not read it would have to assume a value and the only assumable value is the permissive one.

current_password.description: The password the account holds now, proved before anything is changed. It appears in no response body, no error detail and no diagnostic record. A value that is not this account's is `authentication_required` -- the same refusal a missing credential gets, because 'this deployment does not accept this' is one fact.

new_password.description: The password the account will hold. The bounds are mechanical. The deployment enforces a password policy on this operation — a refusal is `validation_failed` and names the rule in `message` — and that policy is not declared here, because it is the deployment's and may differ between them. No history and no expiry are enforced. A value equal to `current_password` is `validation_failed`, because a change that changes nothing would report a password as changed when it was not.

ProjectDocumentCount.description: One row of the "documents per project" panel: the same fact `Project.document_count` already publishes, gathered for every project in one read.

VerdictCount.description: How many findings, across every project, currently stand at one verdict. Every member of `Verdict` is present -- a verdict nobody has recorded is `count: 0`, not an absent row.

RunStateCount.description: How many runs, across every project, currently sit in one state. Every member of `RunState` is present, for the same reason `VerdictCount` states.

RunActivitySpend.description: What every run, across every project, has spent at the provider so far. `cost_basis` is `measured` only when every contributing `model_call` row reported a measured cost.

spend.description: Absent when the deployment has made no provider call.

SectionDocumentCount.description: How many published documents carry one project section (`R-40`, `D-56`). `section` absent means this row is the unclassified bucket, not a fifteenth section. Every one of the fourteen frozen codes is present even at `document_count: 0`.

section.description: One of legacy's fourteen project sections, or absent when the document has not been classified.

DashboardSummary.description: `getDashboardSummary`'s whole answer. All four panels, one read, no filter.

UserUid.description: Opaque account identity. An e-mail address is the sign-in identifier and a unique key among active accounts; this is the identity every reference names.

Role.description: One role an account may hold; an account holds a set of them (R-55, R-60). `expert` makes product changes -- projects, uploads, runs, verdicts, comments and the export. `admin` manages accounts and registration requests. Reading product data needs no role: any active account with a complete profile reads it.

RegistrationStatus.description: The states of the `registration_request` machine in `contracts/domain/v1/state-machines.json`: `pending` until an administrator decides, then `approved` or `rejected`, both terminal.

Account.description: One account, as the account itself reads it through `getMe` and an administrator reads it through the account operations. No credential material.

login.description: The sign-in identifier: the normalised e-mail address (trimmed, lower-case, ASCII, an internationalised domain in its `xn--` form, at most 254 characters) once the profile is complete, or the legacy login an account created before the identity upgrade keeps until it completes its profile. Not an identity of this surface.

display_label.description: The name to show for this account, resolved by the server and never empty: the name form `Last F. M.` when the account has a last and a first name, else the display name an operator chose, else the login. A complete profile always has the name form (R-55).

last_name.description: Null until somebody gives the names.

first_name.description: Null until somebody gives the names.

middle_name.description: Optional; null when the person has none.

roles.description: The role set, sorted. Empty is a valid set: such an account reads product data and changes nothing.

profile_complete.description: False for an account that has not given its names and e-mail yet. Such an account reaches only `getMe`, `updateMyProfile` and `changePassword`; every other operation answers `permission_denied` with `required_capability: profile_completed`.

is_default_credential.description: True while the account must change its password: it is still on the password the deployment seeded it with, or an administrator reset it. The same fact `IssueTokenResponse.is_default_credential` reports at sign-in.

archived_at.description: Null for an active account. An archived account cannot sign in and none of its credentials is accepted; an administrator may restore it.

PersonNames.description: A person's names, set together. 1-60 characters of letters, separated by single spaces, hyphens or apostrophes, with no word mixing Cyrillic and Latin letters. Surrounding whitespace and invisible characters are removed before the rule is applied.

middle_name.description: Optional; absent when the person has none.

UpdateMyProfileRequest.description: The signed-in account's own names, and -- while its profile is incomplete -- the e-mail address that becomes its login. 1-60 characters of letters, separated by single spaces, hyphens or apostrophes, with no word mixing Cyrillic and Latin letters. Surrounding whitespace and invisible characters are removed before the rule is applied.

middle_name.description: Optional; absent when the person has none.

email.description: Required to complete a profile whose login is not yet an e-mail address; it becomes the login in the same write that stores the names. A complete profile's login is fixed: an `email` other than the current login is `validation_failed` with `details.field: login`.

UpdateUserRequest.description: An administrator's change of an account's names, its role set, or both. An absent property leaves that half unchanged.

roles.description: The whole new role set, not a delta. Removing a role from oneself is `permission_denied`; leaving no active account holding `admin` is `conflict` with `details.conflict_reason: last_admin`.

temporary_password.description: The password the account signs in with next and must then change. It is held to the deployment's password policy against the account's login, and it appears in no response body, no error detail and no diagnostic record.

SubmitRegistrationRequest.description: An application for an account. 1-60 characters of letters, separated by single spaces, hyphens or apostrophes, with no word mixing Cyrillic and Latin letters. Surrounding whitespace and invisible characters are removed before the rule is applied.

login.description: The applicant's e-mail address, which becomes the account's login on approval. Normalised by the server (trimmed, lower-case, ASCII, at most 254 characters).

password.description: The account's future password, held to the deployment's password policy with the applicant's names and e-mail local part added to its blocklist. Stored hashed until the decision, which removes it; it appears in no response body, no error detail and no diagnostic record.

middle_name.description: Optional; absent when the person has none.

RegistrationStatusResponse.description: What an applicant is told: that the application is pending. This is the only status this surface ever shows an applicant (R-56 and its addendum of 2026-10-06); a decided application is answered like an unknown pair.

RegistrationRequest.description: One registration request, as an administrator reads it. No credential material.

login.description: The normalised e-mail address the applicant gave.

display_label.description: The applicant's name form, `Last F. M.`, resolved by the server.

middle_name.description: Null when the applicant gave none.

decided_at.description: Null while the request is pending.

decided_by.description: The administrator who decided; null while pending.

rejection_reason.description: The administrator's reason, present only on a rejected request. It is read by administrators only and is never shown to the applicant.

created_user_uid.description: The account an approval created. Null while pending, on a rejected request, and after that account was purged.

RegistrationRequestPage.description: One page of requests and the number of pending requests in all, whatever the filter -- the administrator's badge.

roles.description: The roles the new account receives: at least one.

reason.description: Why the request is rejected, 1-256 characters after surrounding whitespace is removed, with no control character but a line feed. Stored for administrators; the applicant is not shown it.

ProductVersion.description: The running product version from VERSION, its content-derived build identifier, and the unchanged API contract version.

ReleaseNoteKind.description: The editorial category of a release note.

ReleaseNoteItem.description: One user-facing note; where is the navigation label saved at release time.

ReleaseEntry.description: The highest stored revision of one visible release. The archive entry is last; range_label is null for a normal release.

ReleaseList.description: Visible releases newest first, archive last, and the versions this account has not yet read.

MarkReleaseNotesReadRequest.description: The known release version through which this account has read. Unknown or future versions are refused.
